articleSummary: Yellow fever vaccine development began in 1932, marking the start of large-scale use of early vaccines. Initial vaccines were produced by weakening the virus, providing immunity but with drawbacks including encephalitis risk and large serum requirements. In 1937 Max Theiler developed the 17D strain—a safer, more effective vaccine. By 1938 mass vaccination of Brazil employed 17D, establishing it as the global standard. The 1951 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine rewarded Theiler for this discovery. Contemporary vaccination confers lifelong protection for over 99% of recipients with a single dose. Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne acute viral illness; vaccination is the sole preventive measure regulated by the International Health Regulations (2005), which require vaccination documentation for travel to endemic areas. Western Africa saw mass vaccination around 1934, helping drive global adoption in subsequent years.

articleSummary: Bone tuberculosis diagnosed in a 15-year-old boy in Wuhan, Hubei, China, after three months of high fever, red rash, and heel pain. Despite several hospitals, diagnosis remained elusive until admission to Tianyou Hospital (affiliated with Wuhan University of Science and Technology). A non-tender heel 'cold abscess', night fevers, and weight loss prompted metagenomic sequencing, confirming skeletal tuberculosis. The patient also had concurrent bacterial and viral infections and drug allergies. A combined treatment regimen including anti-tuberculosis therapy, anti-infectives, liver protection, and allergy management was started. After two months, fever, rash, and heel pain disappeared; liver function and inflammatory markers improved; MRI showed lesion absorption; he was discharged and returned to school. Bone TB in children can resemble growing pains or juvenile arthritis; persistent local pain, swelling, night sweats, or weight loss, or poor response after 1–2 weeks, warrants early precise testing; most patients recover with timely standard therapy.

articleSummary: The 2026 WHO Global Hepatitis report (Apr 28, 2026) shows measurable progress but ongoing challenge: 287 million people lived with chronic HBV or HCV in 2024; 1.34 million deaths and 1.8 million new infections annually (≈4,900 daily). HBV new infections fell 32% since 2015; HCV-related deaths fell 12%. HBV prevalence among children under five is now 0.6%, with 85 countries achieving/surpassing the 2030 target of 0.1%. Progress is uneven and insufficient to meet all 2030 elimination targets; stigma and weak health systems impede diagnosis and treatment. HBV birth-dose vaccination in the WHO African Region remains only 17%. In 2024, 0.9 million new HBV infections (68% in Africa) and 0.9 million new HCV infections (44% among people who inject drugs). Fewer than 5% of chronic HBV and 20% of HCV infections have been treated since 2015; HCV cure rate exceeds 95% with 8–12 week regimens. HBV deaths cluster in 10 countries (Bangladesh, China, Ethiopia, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Nigeria, Philippines, South Africa, Viet Nam) at 69%; HCV deaths concentrated in China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, South Africa, USA, Viet Nam at 58%. While progress, scale-up of prevention, testing, treatment, and financing is urgently needed to reach 2030 targets.

articleHeadline: Why H2N2 flu is back on the pandemic preparedness radar
articleSummary: Back on pandemic preparedness radar, H2N2 influenza, once dominant in 1957 Asian influenza pandemic, resurges concern due to immunity waning and persistent animal reservoirs. The 1957 H2N2 emerged via reassortment between H1N1 and avian H2N2 in China, spreading globally within months and causing an estimated 1-4 million deaths; it was replaced by H3N2 in 1968. A review of 7 decades of data shows 25 HA mutations, 12 HA1 changes driving antigenic drift, and a shift from α2,3 to α2,6 receptor compatibility, enabling human infection. Current vaccines show promise: two doses of inactivated H2N2 yield 88–100% seroconversion in naïve individuals; ferritin nanoparticle vaccines induce 13–25-fold rise in neutralizing antibodies; a Phase I live-attenuated trial reports 85% antibody and 56% cellular responses. Immunity declines: 100% in 1968 to 15.3% in 2025, projected 2.9% by 2055. Ongoing outbreaks remain possible from animal reservoirs in circulation.
notes: 記事は1957年のH2N2パンデミック発生地としての中国言及と、現在の動物貯蔵池での継続循環を述べている。実際の現在のアウトブレイク報告ではなく、パンデミック準備体制に関する科学的警告・解説記事。ワクチン開発の進展と免疫低下（1968年の100%から2025年の15.3%へ）が述べられており、リスク評価の基盤は存在するが、確認される流行事例がないため WATCH の判定とした。

articleSummary: Dengue is expanding globally, driven by climate change, as researchers deploy single‑cell sequencing and protein biomarker analysis to decode infection, predict severe illness, and guide treatment. The Indo‑EU COMBAT alliance unites Karolinska Institute (Sweden) led by Prof Ujjwal Neogi with Indian partners BRIC‑NIBMG (Kalyani), Regional Centre for Biotechnology (Faridabad), Manipal Institute of Virology (Udupi), Max Hospital (Delhi), and Artemis Hospital (Gurugram) to advance vaccine development and surveillance. Europe’s Horizon funding and India’s DBT support this effort, aiming to strengthen public health infrastructure. DengiAll Phase III trial by ICMR and Panacea Biotec spans 20 sites across 19 Indian states/UTs with over 10,300 participants. Takeda’s TAK‑003 (Qdenga) has been approved in 40+ countries, showing 84.1% efficacy against hospitalized dengue and protection irrespective of prior exposure. ICMR‑NIV Pune pursues antivirals and diagnostics; dengue’s four serotypes and antibody‑dependent enhancement complicate vaccine design.
notes: 記事はインド全域（カルヤーニ、ファリダバード、ウドゥピ、デリー、グルガオン、プネーを含む複数州）でのデング熱拡大と、Indo-EU COMBAT同盟による国際的な研究・ワクチン開発の推進を報告している。ただしサマリーは科学的進展と医療対策の詳細に主眼があり、具体的な患者数・死亡率・流行規模については明記されていない。スウェーデン（カロリンスカ研究所）の関与は記載されているが、スウェーデンでのデング発生は報告されていないため、verified_locationsに含めない。継続的な情報収集により、患者数増加や重症化率の動向を監視すべき。

articleHeadline: Opinion | Evolving threat of 'pink eye' H5N1 bird flu: Could it spread globally?
articleSummary: H5N1 influenza, first identified in Hong Kong in 1999 with 6 of 18 infected dead (≈50% CFR). In Nepal, poultry outbreaks began on eastern-region farms in 2009, and the country later recorded its first human fatality around 2019; a fresh wave of poultry outbreaks is now underway in Nepal. In the United States, human H5N1 infections have been linked to exposure to cattle and raw milk, with conjunctivitis ('pink eye') emerging as a prominent feature. The incubation period ranges from 2–8 days (up to 17); initial fever, cough, and sore throat are common, with shortness of breath around day 5; diarrhea, vomiting, chest pain, and epistaxis have been reported. Pneumonia is a common, fatal complication. No vaccine against H5N1 exists; seasonal vaccines do not cover it. Oseltamivir benefits dairy-exposure cases. Expanded dairy-farm surveillance and epidemiological research are urged; crow die-offs in Kathmandu are noted but not confirmed as linked.
notes: 記事サマリーはネパール、米国、中国（香港含む）の複数国での動向を論じているが、対象国リストに該当するのは中国（香港）のみ。ネパールは対象国外。記事は意見記事（opinion piece）であり、現在のH5N1のグローバルなリスク評価と拡大可能性を論じている。新興臨床症状（結膜炎）、乳製品暴露による感染経路の報告、ワクチン未開発の状況が際立つ。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Swimming with dogs: is there a risk of contracting rabies?
articleHeadline: Bơi chung với chó có nguy cơ mắc dại không?
articleSummary: Rabies is an acute viral CNS infection transmitted to humans mainly through saliva from infected dogs and cats, usually via bites, scratches, or licking of eyes, nose, or mouth. Swimming with dogs is a rare exposure; the virus is inactivated by soap, saltwater, heat, sunlight, and pool chlorine. Frequent dog contact raises risk, especially if children hide injuries or allow dogs to lick mucous membranes. There is no cure once symptoms appear; nearly all cases are fatal. Prevention stresses supervising children around dogs, avoiding rough play, and seeking vaccination after possible exposure. Post-exposure care includes washing wounds with clean water and soap for 15 minutes, then disinfection and vaccination. Vaccines are five intramuscular doses on days 0,3,7,14,28 or four intradermal doses on days 0,3,7,28; immunoglobulin may be added for severe exposure. Do not use folk remedies. Vaccinating pets helps. In Vietnam, Verorab and Abhayrab are safe for all ages; Tây Ninh, Vietnam.
notes: 本記事は狂犬病の感染リスク評価と予防対策に関する一般向けの情報提供記事。具体的な発生事例、患者数、死亡例などの疫学情報は含まれておらず、実際の感染症イベント（アウトブレイク）ではなく、教育的コンテンツである。シグナルトリアージの対象外と判断。

articleHeadline: Preventing Zoonotic Diseases at the Human-Animal Interface in China: Moving
articleSummary: China-wide One Health synthesis in Science in One Health analyzes 93 zoonotic diseases and urges prevention-first strategies at human–animal–environment interfaces. Spillover often stems from everyday activities—smallholder farming, informal food handling, animal trade, and recreational exposure—requiring expanded surveillance into rural and peri-urban settings. Four primary interfaces are highlighted: domestic animals in households/markets; wildlife management in rural areas; synanthropic rodents and bats in residential spaces; and nature-based tourism such as cave exploration. Bat risks are mostly indirect via habitat or livestock; rodent risks via environmental contamination and ectoparasites. Companion and exotic pets are emerging spillover conduits. Blind spots include informal wildlife trade, exotic pet ownership, traditional medicine, and limited granular behavioral data. Risk communication remains reactive; the article advocates community-engaged, trust-based messaging with local leaders, veterinarians, and health workers. China’s SARS/H7N9/COVID-19 history informs proactive, upstream prevention, reinforced by the 2025 Law on Prevention and Control of Infectious Diseases and enhanced One Health data sharing.
notes: 記事は93種類の人獣共通感染症を分析し、中国の過去のSARS/H7N9/COVID-19の履歴を踏まえた予防戦略を論じている。現在の具体的なアウトブレイク情報ではなく、学術的な予防方針の提言である。H7N9とCOVID-19は言及されているが、これらは過去の事例として参照されており、現在の流行状況は記事サマリーには明記されていない。中国政府の2025年感染症予防法改正への言及から政府レベルの関心は高いと判断される。

articleSummary: Russians traveling to South America are advised to vaccinate against yellow fever and use a mosquito repellent with 50% concentration. Vaccination is essential, and travellers should protect themselves from insects, per physician Sergio De Oliveira. The highest risk of yellow fever infection is in Brazil, Bolivia, and Colombia, with Bolivia reporting an outbreak. Yellow fever is an acute viral disease transmitted by mosquitoes, common in tropical Africa and South America. Symptoms include sudden fever, headache, and nausea; severe cases can die within three to four days. There is no specific antiviral treatment. The guidance emphasizes vaccination and preventive measures for travelers before visiting affected regions.

articleHeadlineTranslated: New Imported Measles Cases in São Paulo: Learn the Details.
articleHeadline: Novos casos importados de Sarampo em São Paulo: saiba os detalhes
articleSummary: Two new imported measles cases were confirmed in the capital city of São Paulo, Brazil, on 28 April 2026. One patient is a 42-year-old man resident in Guatemala, and the other a six-month-old unvaccinated infant with a travel link to Bolivia earlier this year. Measles is a highly contagious viral disease that can cause severe complications, especially in young children and young adults; vaccination is the most effective prevention. Despite Brazil’s PAHO-elimination status in 2020, imported cases and gaps in vaccination heighten the risk of renewed transmission. The Health Ministry urges updating vaccination records, with the measles-mumps-rubella (triple viral) vaccine given at 12 and 15 months. Preventive measures include early case identification, isolation, and contact tracing, reinforced by strengthened surveillance, health‑worker training, clear public information, and intergovernmental collaboration to prevent reintroduction.

articleHeadlineTranslated: East Kutai Regency Government targets tuberculosis elimination by 2030.
articleHeadline: Pemkab Kutai Timur targetkan eliminasi penyakit TB pada 2030 - ANTARA News Kalimantan Timur
articleSummary: TB elimination targeted by 2030 in East Kutai Regency, Kalimantan Timur (Indonesia), with the Kutai Timur government engaging PPTI (Tuberculosis Eradication Association of Indonesia) and district-level PACs. In Sangatta, Kutai Timur, about 1,000 TB patients are spread across 18 districts. PAC cadres will assist in data collection, case finding, and active reporting to guide precise interventions. The initiative aims to interrupt transmission, reduce new cases, and protect vulnerable groups—children, pregnant women, the elderly, and those with weakened immune systems. Officials urge community involvement, healthy living, clean environments, and avoidance of smoking as risk reduction. PPTI chair Siti Robiah Ardiansyah says establishing PACs in all 18 districts broadens prevention, case finding, and treatment support. Success depends on case reporting, complete treatment, and sustained public health measures.
